title: Roman carnelian intaglio (Mars?) from Khao Sam Kaeo
language_note: Scholarly excavation/gemological report in English (Bérénice Bellina et al. excavation project); no inscribed text on the object itself, which is a carved gemstone.
date: mid-2nd to early 3rd century CE (Roman production); Khao Sam Kaeo site occupied 4th-3rd century BCE onward
findspot: Khao Sam Kaeo, Chumphon Province, upper Thai-Malay Peninsula, Thailand
original_text_excerpt: A Roman intaglio, yellow carnelian, depicting a standing figure, probably Mars, dressed in military costume with a crested helmet. Lacks secure stratigraphic context, but provenance from the site is not doubted.
original_text_note: Description drawn from Borell/Hoppal gemological studies of Roman engraved gems from Southeast Asia; treat as the closest 'original text' available for this artefact record.
notes: Khao Sam Kaeo is an early port-city (4th century BCE onward) on the trans-peninsular route linking the Indian Ocean to the South China Sea, and yielded South Asian seals alongside this Roman intaglio — direct physical evidence of the same Indian-Ocean exchange network documented textually in the South Asia cluster (Periplus, Muziris papyrus). Good candidate for a 'maritime route' graph edge spanning South Asia and Southeast Asia.

findspot_places.name: Khao Sam Kaeo
findspot_places.note: **GeoNames 8242723 'Khao Sam Kaeo' was examined and REFUSED on coordinate.** It is a T.HLL (hill) at 8.016/100.191 — 297 km south of Chumphon, in a different province from the site this record describes. *Khao Sam Kaeo* is a generic Thai toponym (roughly 'three-crystal hill') and the name matches a hill that is not this one; accepting it would have drawn the Thai-Malay peninsular trade site 300 km down the coast. Same class of error as Byzantion on the Konkan, and caught the same way — on the coordinate, not the name. The archaeological site at Khao Sam Kaeo, on the Tha Tapao river near Chumphon town, has no entry in the GeoNames TH dump under this name, and none in Pleiades. What is known is the region: the upper Thai-Malay peninsula, Chumphon Province. No point is drawn, which is correct.
